text: Code review happens on the Files changed tab. Hovering over any line in the diff reveals a blue plus button — click it to attach a comment to that exact line, instead of a vague note on the PR as a whole.
Anchoring feedback to the precise line it concerns is the whole value of an inline comment — the author doesn't have to guess which part of a two-hundred-line diff you mean.

On a large PR, a Viewed checkbox next to each file lets you mark your way through the diff and collapse files you've already looked at. It resets if the author pushes new commits to a file you'd already checked off.

Once you've gone through the diff, Review changes submits your verdict. Comment leaves feedback with no formal verdict. Approve signals you're satisfied. Request changes explicitly blocks the merge until it's addressed.
The best review comments are specific and actionable, and say clearly whether something's a nitpick or a blocker. Next up: tracking the work itself, with issues and project boards.
